findings.title: intcomma skips grouping for signed negative numbers
findings.cause: The separator loop applies re.sub(r"^(\d+)(\d{3})", ...) to the whole formatted string, so any leading minus sign prevents the integer part from ever matching.
findings.impact: Negative integers, floats, and numeric strings are returned without thousands separators, which breaks the function contract for common monetary and count values and also affects locale-formatted output.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:164-174 formats to a string, then only inserts separators when the string starts with digits.
tests/test_number.py:41-83 covers positive intcomma inputs and non-finite values but no negative finite inputs.
Focused probe: intcomma(-1234) actual='-1234' expected='-1,234'; intcomma('-1234.56') actual='-1234.56' expected='-1,234.56'.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add assertions to test_intcomma: assert humanize.intcomma(-1234) == '-1,234' and assert humanize.intcomma('-1234.56') == '-1,234.56'.

findings.title: clamp marks exact floor and ceil values as out of range
findings.cause: The implementation clamps with value <= floor and value >= ceil, while the docstring and argument docs describe only values smaller than the floor or larger than the ceil as token-worthy.
findings.impact: Exact threshold values get misleading under/over labels such as >99% or <1%, which can invert boundary semantics in dashboards, reports, and validation messaging.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:464-475 says larger than ceil/smaller than floor are clamped and documents clamp(0.99, ceil=0.99) -> 99%.
src/humanize/number.py:509-514 uses <= and >=, adding tokens at equality.
tests/test_number.py:223-240 tests below/above thresholds but omits exact floor/ceil equality.
Focused probe: clamp(0.99, format="{:.0%}", ceil=0.99) actual='>99%' expected='99%'; clamp(0.01, floor=0.01) actual='<1%' expected='1%'.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add equality cases to test_clamp for floor and ceil, e.g. assert humanize.clamp(0.99, format='{:.0%}', ceil=0.99) == '99%'.

findings.title: fractional loses or duplicates the sign for negative fractions
findings.cause: The function truncates toward zero with int(number), then builds the fractional remainder from number - whole_number; for pure negative fractions it calls abs(numerator), and for mixed negatives it prints the negative numerator after a negative whole number.
findings.impact: Negative fractional values are not data-preserving: -0.5 becomes positive 1/2, and -1.5 becomes the awkward double-negative string -1 -1/2.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:370-382 computes the remainder from the signed number and applies abs only in the no-whole-number branch.
tests/test_number.py:166-189 covers positive fractions and non-finite values but no negative finite fractions.
Focused probe: fractional(-0.5) actual='1/2' expected='-1/2'; fractional(-1.5) actual='-1 -1/2' expected='-1 1/2'.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add negative cases to test_fractional: assert humanize.fractional(-0.5) == '-1/2' and assert humanize.fractional(-1.5) == '-1 1/2'.

findings.title: naturalsize crashes or invents byte units for non-finite floats
findings.cause: naturalsize converts to float and immediately uses log(abs_bytes, base) without a finite check, unlike the number helpers that route NaN and infinities through _format_not_finite.
findings.impact: NaN raises ValueError and infinities format as inf QB or -inf QB, so callers formatting calculation results or untrusted numeric input can crash or display a bogus finite filesize unit.
evidence: src/humanize/filesize.py:89-101 converts to float, compares sizes, then computes int(min(log(...))) without math.isfinite handling.
tests/test_filesize.py:12-96 covers ordinary positive/negative sizes but no nan/inf inputs.
Focused probe: naturalsize(math.nan) raised ValueError; naturalsize(math.inf) actual='inf QB' expected='+Inf' for consistency with other numeric helpers.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add non-finite cases to test_naturalsize, e.g. assert humanize.naturalsize(math.nan) == 'NaN', assert humanize.naturalsize(math.inf) == '+Inf', assert humanize.naturalsize(-math.inf) == '-Inf'.

findings.title: naturaldelta and naturaltime leak OverflowError for numeric infinity
findings.cause: naturaldelta catches ValueError and TypeError around int(value) and timedelta construction, but int(math.inf) raises OverflowError. naturaltime also reaches unchecked OverflowError through round(value) in _date_and_delta for numeric infinity.
findings.impact: The documented fallback for values that cannot be converted due to inf/nan is inconsistent: string NaN is returned unchanged, but numeric infinity can crash relative-time formatting.
evidence: src/humanize/time.py:112-116 documents that values that cannot be converted to int due to 'inf' or 'nan' are returned unchanged.
src/humanize/time.py:86-90 and 148-153 catch ValueError/TypeError but not OverflowError.
tests/test_time.py:120-136 and 170-187 include string NaN but no math.inf case.
Focused probe: naturaldelta(math.inf) and naturaltime(math.inf) both raised OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add tests for math.inf and -math.inf in test_naturaldelta/test_naturaltime, deciding whether they should return str(value) or use the shared +Inf/-Inf formatting convention.
